sections.note: "Race in Europe" explores notions of race, radicalization, racism, and racelessness in the European Context, broadly-defined. With an interdisciplinary approach that incorporates perspectives from sociology, anthropology, history, European studies, Black studies, Roma studies, and beyond, as well as knowledge you bring from your own studies and experiences, we will gain deeper understanding of both the theory surrounding these notions and their application to various populations in Europe. We will also spend some time throughout the semester situating what we learn within our existing schemas around race and race relations born out of our own diverse backgrounds. This course is delivered in a hybrid format with a weekly asynchronous online lecture and relevant homework on each week's topic to be completed before each weekly in-person discussion-based meeting.

sections.note: LLanguage & Minorities in Europe. Credit: 3 or 4 hours. Survey of regional and immigrant minority language use, policies, and planning across Europe. Focus on political and social issues, such as language regimes, education, loss, and maintenance. Two immigrant languages, Turkish and Arabic/Berber, and four indigenous language families: Balto-Slavic with Estonian, Celtic, Romance with Basque, and Slavic with Hungarian. Taught in English. Same as GER 418, ITAL 418, LING 418, PS 418, SLAV 418, SPAN 418, and EURO 418. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

Political Leadership and European Integration: From Robert Schuman in the immediate aftermath of the 2nd World War to Ursula von der Leyen in 2025, political leaders at the helm of various European nation-states or EU institutions have been central to the ongoing project to integrate Europe. This course broadly examines the dynamic and complex relationship between political leadership on the one side and European integration on the other. Topics covered include, among other things, multi-level decision-making by European political leaders, the impact of leadership styles on EU governance, case studies of key leaders especially as they relate to mechanisms, processes, and effects of European integration, as well as theories of European integration. Applicable course for Undergraduate Certificate in EU Studies. Counts toward MAEUS degree or Graduate Minor in EU Studies.

sections.note: This seminar is a roundtable exploring a variety of topics related to Europe, transatlantic relations, the European Union, and the peripheries. Students will have an opportunity to participate in regular conversations about current issues ranging from cultural policies, migration, economic policies, bureaucratic politics, international security, sports, popular culture, and other topics of high salience to Europe and the European Union. Opportunities for guest speakers and readings on professionalization. Open to undergraduate and graduate students. Required core class for Undergraduate Certificate in EU Studies. Counts toward MAEUS degree or Graduate Minor in EU Studies.

title: The EU in a Global Context

sections.note: The EU in Global Context focuses on the interests of European Union and Europe in global perspective. Topics examined include historical issues of identity, foreign policy, and global networks. The course asks several broad questions: How are the global actions of the European Union a continuation of the long-term ambitions of European societies? How do these actions diverge from historical narratives and patterns? How is the EU's global influence best understood? How do actors from around the world approach interactions with individuals, organizations and institutions within the European Union?
